sections.heading: Eligibility for the scheme
sections.summary: All four criteria apply. You must own and live in the home as your main residence, it must have been built and occupied before 2006, you must receive a qualifying welfare payment, and a survey must find the home suitable for improvements.
details: Qualifying payments include Fuel Allowance under the National Fuel Scheme, Working Family Payment, One-Parent Family Payment, and Domiciliary Care Allowance.
Carer's Allowance qualifies if you live with the person you care for. SEAI asks for its confirmation form.
Jobseeker's Allowance or Disability Allowance qualifies if you have received it for more than six months and have a child under seven. SEAI asks for the child's birth certificate.

sections.heading: How to apply
sections.summary: Apply via the online form linked by SEAI or use its paper application form. Have your electricity meter point reference number (MPRN), proof of home ownership and any documents required for your circumstances.
details: Check the documents listed on the official page before submitting. SEAI confirms eligibility and assesses the property before deciding which upgrades are suitable.
Apartment applicants need management company permission before assessments or works proceed.

sections.heading: Application stages
sections.summary: SEAI describes a pre-works Building Energy Rating assessment, a home survey, approved works by an assigned contractor, and a final rating assessment with an inspection in some cases.

sections.heading: Who can apply
sections.summary: The property needs an MPRN and must have been built and occupied before 2011. SEAI lists owner-occupiers, first-time buyers and several other ownership categories.

sections.heading: Grants values for attic insulation
sections.summary: Standard amounts depend on dwelling type.
details: Apartment €1,100, mid-terrace €1,400, semi-detached or end-terrace €1,500, detached €2,000.
Enhanced amounts for eligible applicants are €1,400, €1,800, €1,900 and €2,500 respectively. Check the specific first-time buyer, qualifying welfare payment or active HAP/RAS conditions.

sections.heading: How to apply
sections.summary: Choose a contractor registered for the measure and get SEAI approval before starting. Apply online or by post.
details: Accept the offer within 30 days. Allow for completion, the post-works BER and paperwork within eight months of the offer.

sections.heading: Who can apply
sections.summary: SEAI requires an MPRN and specifies that the home must have been built and occupied before 31 December 2010. The grant requires insulating the full external wall surface.
details: A previous cavity grant can be followed by internal or external insulation. A previous internal grant can be followed by external insulation. A prior external grant rules out a second wall measure.

sections.heading: Grants values for wall insulation
sections.summary: The amount depends on the dwelling and insulation method. Values below are in cavity, internal and external order.
details: Enhanced cavity support ranges from €900 to €2,300 by dwelling type for eligible welfare or active HAP/RAS cases.

sections.heading: How to apply
sections.summary: For a self-managed project, use a contractor registered for the measure and secure SEAI approval before work starts.

sections.heading: Eligibility criteria
sections.summary: The home must have been built and occupied before 2011 and have sufficient attic and wall insulation. Check the existing BER advisory report or consult a BER assessor.
details: Eligible work replaces existing single or double glazing with high-performing windows or replaces inefficient external doors.

sections.heading: Grant values
sections.summary: Window grant by dwelling: apartment €1,500, mid-terrace €1,800, semi-detached or end-terrace €3,000, detached €4,000.
details: External doors qualify for €800 each, up to two. Windows and doors may be applied for individually or together.

sections.heading: Grant payment criteria
sections.summary: Payment requires a post-works BER, replacement units meeting a U-value of 1.4 W/(m²·K) or lower, and either a heat loss indicator of 2.3 W/(m²·K) or lower or qualifying attic and wall ratings in the advisory report.
details: The work must meet SEAI's ventilation and safety requirements. Multiple doors claimed together must use the same appointed registered contractor.

sections.heading: How to apply
sections.summary: Get quotes from registered contractors, apply to SEAI and wait for the grant offer before starting under the standard process.
details: SEAI's FAQ describes a transitional exception for certain recently ordered or commenced work. Check the FAQ before ruling out such a case.

sections.heading: Who can apply
sections.summary: The home needs an MPRN and must have been built and occupied before 2021.

sections.heading: Grant values for heat pump systems
sections.summary: The maximum bundle can reach €14,500 depending on dwelling type and eligibility. It combines up to €10,500 for the unit, up to €2,000 for required distribution upgrades and up to €2,000 for qualifying heating replacement or installation.
details: A separate replacement route applies to existing heat pumps that never received an SEAI domestic grant. Maximum €6,500, or €4,500 for apartments.

sections.heading: Technical assessment for heat loss
sections.summary: For pre-2007 homes a technical assessment is required unless a valid BER shows a heat loss indicator of 2.3 W/(m²·K) or below. Homes built from 2007 can use the self-declaration route.
details: Upload the applicable assessment or declaration with the application.

sections.heading: How to apply
sections.summary: Use an SEAI-registered contractor for the measure and get grant approval before starting work.

sections.heading: Who can apply
sections.summary: Homeowners, including private landlords, owner management companies and approved housing bodies can apply. The home needs an MPRN, must have been built and occupied before 2025, and must have no previous solar PV funding at that MPRN.

sections.heading: Grant value for solar electricity
sections.summary: The standard solar PV grant pays €700 per kWp for the first 2 kWp and €200 per additional kWp up to 4 kWp. The PV maximum is €1,800.
details: A qualifying 5 kWh battery may add €600. SEAI lists separate enhanced supports for certain welfare recipients and the Dublin RAS pilot.

sections.heading: How to apply
sections.summary: Choose an SEAI-registered solar PV company and get an offer before work begins. Complete the works and submit documents within eight months of approval.

sections.heading: About the new low-cost loan
sections.summary: SEAI lists loans from €5,000 to €75,000 for up to 10 years. Participating lenders set their own rates and make the lending decision.

sections.heading: Eligibility criteria
sections.summary: The owner must be upgrading a property in the Republic of Ireland through a qualifying SEAI grant with a registered One Stop Shop or Community Project Coordinator.
details: Eligible energy work after deducting the grant must account for at least 75% of the loan. The projected energy performance improvement must be at least 20%. Completed projects are excluded.

sections.heading: How to apply
sections.summary: Ask the registered provider for a Home Energy Summary Report, then apply to a participating lender listed by SBCI. Check current lender terms before relying on the figures.

sections.heading: Check your eligibility
sections.summary: The home must have been built and occupied before 2011. After work, it must reach at least a B BER and either have a heat pump installed or achieve a primary energy improvement of 100 kWh/m² per year.
details: SEAI lists homeowners, first-time buyers, private landlords and approved housing bodies. The provider checks your project's technical eligibility.

sections.heading: Exclusions
sections.summary: Previous SEAI funding for the same measures or energy credits through EEOS can affect eligibility. Ask your provider to check the specific measures.

sections.heading: What to expect from a One Stop Shop
sections.summary: The provider arranges the assessment, manages the grant applications and work, and arranges the post-works BER. It deducts the grants upfront from the cost charged to you.
details: An SEAI grant of €350 is available for a home energy assessment carried out by a One Stop Shop.

sections.heading: 3.1 Find a contractor
sections.summary: For an individual home energy grant, choose a contractor registered with SEAI for the exact work you plan to do. Search by county, service area and measure using the official register.
details: Solar PV has a separate registered company list. For a managed home retrofit, use the registered One Stop Shop list.
SEAI registration sets requirements for participating contractors. SEAI does not guarantee their work.

sections.heading: 3.2 Getting the best results with your chosen contractor
sections.summary: Compare quotes, ask for references and get a written contract before proceeding.
details: Check that the contract specifies the work, price, timing, payment terms and warranties.

officialLinks.label: Find a registered solar PV company
Find a registered One Stop Shop

sections.heading: Grant value
sections.summary: SEAI offers a flat €600 grant for a home battery with a capacity of at least 5 kWh.

sections.heading: Who can apply
sections.summary: Homeowners, including private landlords, owner management companies and approved housing bodies can apply. The home needs an MPRN and must have been built and occupied before 2025.
details: A property that has already received battery grant funding is ineligible.

sections.heading: Battery and Solar PV
sections.summary: If you are installing both measures, you can apply for both grants in one application. If a solar PV application is already open, submit a new application for the battery.

sections.heading: Criteria
sections.summary: Use an SEAI-registered solar PV contractor and wait for your grant offer before installing the battery.
details: A post-works BER is required if the home has solar PV.

sections.heading: Grant value for solar water heating
sections.summary: SEAI offers €1,200 for solar thermal hot water, regardless of the property type.

sections.heading: Who can apply
sections.summary: The property needs an MPRN and must have been built and occupied before 2025. Eligible owners include owner-occupiers, holiday-home owners and certain landlords and organisations.

sections.heading: 2. Apply to SEAI for grant offer
sections.summary: Choose a contractor registered with SEAI for solar thermal, then apply online or by post and wait for approval before work begins.
details: Have the contractor’s name and ID, the property's MPRN, its dwelling type and its year of construction and first occupation. Accept the offer within 30 days.

sections.heading: Difference between a Home Energy Assessment and a BER
sections.summary: A BER rates your home’s energy performance and is a starting point if you are planning one or two upgrades. A Home Energy Assessment includes a BER and a technical report for planning a larger retrofit.

sections.heading: About your assessment
sections.summary: A One Stop Shop assessment can set out the upgrades needed to reach a B rating or better, estimated costs and what would make the home suitable for a heat pump.

sections.heading: Grant for a home energy assessment
sections.summary: SEAI contributes €350 once per property. The One Stop Shop claims the grant and deducts it from the assessment price.
details: Assessment prices vary. Compare quotes from registered One Stop Shops.

title: Retrofitting a traditional or heritage home

sections.heading: Eligibility for the traditional homes pilot
sections.summary: The pilot supports whole-home upgrades for owners of traditionally built properties, typically built before 1940. Engage a Traditional Building Professional and a registered One Stop Shop that provides traditional-home services.
details: The same measures must not have received previous SEAI grant support.

sections.heading: Exclusions
sections.summary: Projects already under way and proposals for a single upgrade are ineligible. You cannot claim both SEAI support and the Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant for the same works.

sections.heading: Apply for the pilot programme
sections.summary: The One Stop Shop manages the retrofit and grant application. Agree a retrofit suitable for the building’s construction and heritage with your professional and One Stop Shop, and confirm the scheme’s technical criteria with them before proceeding.

sections.heading: Grant for complete home upgrade to minimum BER B
sections.summary: Private landlords can use a registered One Stop Shop for a managed upgrade involving multiple measures. SEAI says the home must reach at least a B rating and the provider deducts the grant from the price.

sections.heading: Individual energy grants for step-by-step upgrades
sections.summary: Private and commercial landlords can apply for eligible measures and use a contractor registered with SEAI. Check the individual measure for property and applicant rules.
details: SEAI directs commercial landlords to obtain the relevant authorisation forms before applying for a Better Energy Homes grant.

sections.heading: Enhanced grants for HAP and RAS-supported properties
sections.summary: Landlords with an active Housing Assistance Payment tenancy or Rental Accommodation Scheme arrangement may qualify for enhanced support on eligible measures. Check the criteria for the grant you plan to claim.

title: Energy grants for vacant and derelict homes

sections.heading: About the scheme
sections.summary: A vacant-home renovation can combine the local authority’s Vacant Property Refurbishment Grant with SEAI support for separate work. You can claim only one grant for any given item of work.

sections.heading: Applying to the grant scheme
sections.summary: Tell the local authority Grant Officer if you are applying for both schemes. Choose the SEAI grant route that fits the energy upgrades you are planning and apply through that route.

title: Higher energy grants for homeowners on qualifying welfare payments

sections.heading: Are you in receipt of any of the following DSP welfare payments?
sections.summary: Check SEAI’s list of qualifying payments. These include Fuel Allowance under the National Fuel Scheme, Working Family Payment, One-Parent Family Payment and Domiciliary Care Allowance.
details: Carer’s Allowance qualifies if you live with the person you care for. Jobseeker’s Allowance or Disability Allowance qualifies after more than six months if you have a child under seven.

sections.heading: Choose the grant route that is right for you
sections.summary: Enhanced individual grants let you choose eligible upgrades and a registered contractor. With Warmer Homes, SEAI assesses the home, selects suitable measures and manages and funds the approved work.
details: The managed route has its own eligibility rules, including a home built and occupied before 2006.
